{{Short description|Module generated by a countable subset}}
In [[mathematics]], a [[module (mathematics)|module]] over a (not necessarily [[commutative ring|commutative]]) [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] is '''countably generated''' if it is [[generating set of a module|generated]] as a module by a [[countable]] subset. The importance of the notion comes from [[Kaplansky's theorem on projective modules|Kaplansky's theorem]] (Kaplansky 1958), which states that a [[projective module]] is a [[direct sum of modules|direct sum]] of countably generated modules.

More generally, a module over a possibly [[non-commutative ring|non-commutative]] ring is projective [[if and only if]] (i) it is [[flat module|flat]], (ii) it is a direct sum of countably generated modules and (iii) it is a [[Mittag-Leffler module]]. (Bazzoni–Stovicek)
